article.title: Nolan Well
article.author: Melina Abdullah
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Do you think that in such a short time you can persuade me to be a Christian? Acts 26:28 Christian Anthony Claudio is a righteous young Black man of conscience from upstate New York. He is a central fixture in his family and tightly-knit community, where he works with special needs children and can be relied on to help friends when their cars break down. At just 25-years-old, he owns his own home, pays his own bills, has never been arrested, and stands as a model of what it means to be a good brother, son, friend, and neighbor. He lives up to his name – Christian. Christian saw himself in Nolan Wells, the 18-year-old son of Christine and Elmore Wonsley, a college athlete, who loved his parents and siblings, a friend to all and an enemy of none. Nolan was killed this past July 4th in the midst of an all white “friend” group in Mississippi. When the entire Mississippi system of (in)justice refused to prosecute anyone for Nolan’s death, instead calling his death an “accidental drowning,” from 1200 miles away, Christian took what action he could. He called the court clerk in Jackson County, Mississippi and asked why. For that simple act, Christian has been charged with making terroristic threats, arrested, jailed for weeks in New York, then extradited to Jackson County, Mississippi, the same county that is covering up the murder of Nolan Wells. Related: Black Lives Matter LA Has 10 Demands for Mayor-Elect Nithya Raman There is no publicly available recording of Christian’s call. The sole public record of the alleged threat is an affidavit of Jackson County Detective Justin Quinnelly. Social media reports are swirling: that the clerk who received the call is the sheriff’s wife, that she’s friends with Judge Ashlee Cole – the stepmother of one of the white boys embroiled in the killing of Nolan Wells, that the sheriff has a long history of putting Black folks “in their place.” Christian is now the sixth person charged for asking questions about the death of Nolan Wells. Others, from Illinois and California also have pending cases. NFL star Terrell Owens is being sued for posting about the case, declaring that those involved should be arrested. You know who hasn’t been charged or suffered any negative repercussions? Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo, and Morgan Seymour…the white “friends”…sons of judges and of the confederacy. They have gone on with their lives, protected by a system designed to do just that, and crowdfunded to the tune of almost a quarter million dollars. This is the devil’s work carried by Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch, who said that the investigation of Nolan’s death would be left to the local District Attorney, but any “tampering” would be handled by her office. The same Attorney General who deemed the murder of 1-year-old Baby #KohenWiley by Senatobia police “justified,” who signed off on the murder of #JaylenLewis by Mississippi Capitol police, refused charges in at least 20 more Black people killed by police, and paid restitution to the cop who killed #GeorgeRobinson. Fitch is the same Attorney General whose family is preserving the home of the first Grand Wizard of the Ku Klux Klan on their plantation land. Fitch has announced her run for Mississippi Governor in 2028. Related: Representation Is Not Liberation: Why I Vote My Values, Not My Loyalties Fitch’s reign does not go unchallenged. Ms. Bettersten Wade, mother of #DexterWade and sister of #GeorgeRobinson – both killed by Jackson police, holds regular protests at Fitch’s office and Jackson People’s Assembly has been carrying the long and hard work for years. Black Lives Matter Youth Vanguard member, Jerome Richardson, who himself was arrested with charges pending for being present during an anti-ICE action at a church in St. Paul, Minnesota (along with journalists Georgia Fort, Don Lemon, attorney Nekima Levy-Armstrong, BLM Grassroots organizers Chauntyll Allen, Satara Strong, and 30 others), has thrown himself into the unseen work of organizing for Christian Claudio’s release. Grassroots activists from Mississippi’s gulf coast are standing strong to ensure Christian’s safe return home. Black Lives Matter Grassroots supporters have pitched in to ensure that there are funds for his bond, travel, and care. Even a Black bailbondswoman has stepped up, cutting her fees to ensure that Christian is released quickly and safely. On Tuesday, Black students at UCLA are protesting for Nolan Wells. This weekend Latinx allies are rallying in Mariachi Plaza for Nolan Wells and Baby #KohenWiley, who was killed by police outside a Walmart in Senatobia, Mississippi. On Friday, in Mississippi, Ms. Bettersten will lead another protest outside Lynn Fitch’s office. Nolan Wells’ parents have asked us to keep saying his name. We must and we will. Christian’s next courtdate is in February. Conditions of his release include an ankle monitor and no posting on social media. But they cannot quiet all of us. We must continue to fight for Nolan, for Kohen, and for all of our people…in Mississippi and everywhere. Forces of evil have arrested one, but let a million Christians be inspired to do good and righteous work. Los Angeles Sentinel
